comparator.name: Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum totals 180 ECTS. Years 1 and 2 each contain 60 ECTS of microeconomics, macroeconomics, quantitative methods, programming, finance and applied economic analysis. Year 3 comprises a 30-ECTS mobility/minor/internship window, 12 ECTS of electives chosen from the published list, a 6-ECTS philosophy-and-history course and a 12-ECTS thesis. Zero-credit GROW activity is excluded; genuine choice space is not filled with assumed courses.

alternatives.label: Economics, policy & quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres economic theory, policy and data analysis rather than business administration, making its organising logic explicit without claiming Tilburg’s full specialist sequence.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible response combining micro- and macroeconomics with public economics, international economics, statistics, data, econometrics and supporting finance and institutions.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, mathematical and strategic foundations precede the advanced policy, organisational, international-business, machine-learning, econometrics, behavioural-economics, market-research and finance work. Strategy follows Business Foundations; Probability & Statistics follows Mathematical Methods; Money, Banking & Finance follows business, accounting and economic study. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.
traceOverrides: provides multivariate statistics and experimental methods that strengthen empirical economic and business research

alternatives.label: Public economics, institutions & inequality
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum makes public economics, political institutions, law, inequality and policy research its organising emphasis while retaining economics and quantitative foundations.
alternatives.concept: An economics-and-public-policy direction combining markets, macroeconomics and econometrics with political institutions, law, inequality, governance, social theory and policy research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces accounting, marketing, business strategy, international business, product design, machine learning, probability and finance with comparative politics, sociology, qualitative methods, political philosophy, human rights, constitutional law, sustainability governance, EU politics, social theory, persuasive communication, peace and conflict, and historical research. The resulting curriculum is organised around institutions and policy rather than firms and business functions.
progression: Foundational economics, politics and sociology precede advanced public economics, governance, constitutional law, EU politics, social theory, policy communication and research. Qualitative Research Methodology precedes the final research seminar; Research Methods & Statistics precedes econometrics. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

alternatives.label: Financial economics & quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around finance and economics with substantial mathematics, programming, data, econometrics and optimisation, rather than implying a specialist finance degree without a quantitative core.
alternatives.concept: A financial-economics direction combining money, banking and finance with micro- and macroeconomics, econometrics, probability, calculus, programming, databases, machine learning and optimisation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It therefore retains the economics and business core while making quantitative financial and economic analysis the organising emphasis. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.
progression: Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation and Money, Banking & Finance. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics, Linear Algebra and Advanced Calculus; programming precedes computational decision-making; accounting, economics, data and research foundations precede the final finance, econometrics and behavioural-economics work. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

candidates.label: Public economics, institutions, inequality and data power

selection.assessment: The closest curriculum covers the programme-wide microeconomic, macroeconomic and quantitative core. Public economics/institutions/inequality and financial economics each support coherent, mechanically feasible and substantially distinct UCR alternatives. Behavioral and experimental economics is a further evidenced direction, but no fourth alternative can be included.

blocks: UCR Introduction to Economics introduces both micro- and macroeconomics; this row aligns it only with Tilburg’s introductory microeconomics component.
Both examine welfare, market efficiency, uncertainty and behavioural choice; Tilburg’s course is the dedicated welfare-economics component.
Both examine international macroeconomics, capital flows and policy; Tilburg’s course is explicitly international finance.
Both examine taxation, redistribution, public goods, market failure and public policy.
Both study strategic and behavioural economic decision-making; UCR is broader than dedicated game theory.
UCR International Macroeconomics overlaps but does not reproduce Tilburg’s dedicated business-cycles-and-crises course.
Both provide accounting and financial foundations; UCR additionally covers corporate finance.
Both develop finance, investment and risk analysis; UCR also covers money and banking.
Both address international economic and institutional relationships; UCR approaches them through business and governance rather than a dedicated trade model sequence.
Both examine economic power and decision-making in data-intensive environments; UCR centres AI and business.
Both provide mathematical techniques for economic and quantitative modelling; UCR is broader and less economics-specific.
Both provide statistics and empirical-analysis foundations; UCR combines them with broader research design.
Both develop econometric estimation, testing and empirical analysis.
Both introduce programming for analytical problem-solving; UCR uses Python.
UCR Introduction to Economics is already shown once and is not duplicated as a separate macroeconomics match.
UCR has programming but no separate R-programming course in these alternatives.
UCR has microeconomics and public economics but no dedicated industrial-economics course.
UCR has macroeconomics and institutional study but no dedicated growth-and-institutions course.
UCR develops data and communication skills across courses but lacks this dedicated integration.
UCR includes development and inequality questions across courses but no dedicated Development Economics course.
Both support reflective competence and professional development; UCR is broader personal and professional development.
Both develop ethical and philosophical reflection, though Tilburg focuses specifically on science and free markets.
The comparator’s genuine mobility, internship or minor space is not populated with assumed courses.
UCR Ethics does not reproduce the dedicated history-of-economic-thought component.
The comparator’s two-course elective choice remains open rather than assumed.
UCR optional independent research is shown separately and does not make the Tilburg thesis a direct course match.

notes.text: Tilburg requires a sustained economics sequence spanning welfare, international finance, game theory, industrial economics, growth, development, communication with data and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can build coherent economics pathways, but it does not reproduce that full specialist sequence.
